prose_updates.tldr: For an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty stratum set \(S\), a common holdout fraction \(\rho\) indexes a chronological two-stage enrichment randomization and its same-design Fisher sharp-null reference. Stage-one randomized action is the pair of holdout and treatment vectors; this gives a formal specialization of Freidling--Zhao--Gao's augmented-action representation, with their Proposition 1 supplying validity independently of imputability and Proposition 2 supplying computability at the sharp null. A per-array common remainder transfers the shifted sampling cdf and the zero-drift data-dependent reference cdf on every complete signed cell. Finite-product factorization reduces each active cell to a scalar selected Gaussian power. Ehrhard--Borell convexity reduces arbitrary compact positive alternatives to their least coordinate, the sign of \(\Delta_j=A_s-\kappa_jb_{1j}\) fixes the side of the proportional stage weight, all nonnegative discrepancies force the largest holdout, and an explicit two-stratum mixture certifies an interior negative-discrepancy regime. Mixed signs have a complete equality-aware analytic branch characterization, while interval computation returns certified value and optimizer-set boxes and asserts uniqueness only with separation.

project_justification.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao provide a broader adaptive-experiment validity and conditional-reference framework, but do not derive a finite-population selected Gaussian power limit or optimize a common holdout and cell-specific stage weights. Existing finite-population central limit theorems are unconditional, and Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu study nonnested normal model-based policies with a different expected-sample-size and familywise-error objective. None supplies the present field-level sampling/reference transfer and maximin conditional-power frontier over arbitrary fixed finite strata.
project_justification.niche: The missing design object is a fixed-finite-stratum, design-based maximin problem in which one scalar holdout changes both selection and retained first-stage information, while each active complete-cell coordinate has its own nonnegative unit-norm stage weight. The optimizer can be an endpoint, an interior point, or a set-valued mixed-sign correspondence.
project_justification.fill: The project embeds the stage-one action as \(\widetilde Z_{n1si}=(D_{nsi},Z_{n1si})\), with \(D_{nsi}=\mathbf 1\{i\in H_{n,s}\}\), duplicates potential outcomes across the holdout label, and verifies the FZG A1--A3 and same-selector resampling equations. At the sharp null, Proposition 2 computes the explicit chronological reference and Proposition 1 separately transfers exact validity. The new contribution then derives, for arbitrary fixed finite \(S\), a common per-array split-conditional Gaussian and reference transfer, scalar complete-cell power integrals, least-coordinate reduction, the \(\Delta\)-indexed weight theorem, a unique largest-holdout region, a certified two-stratum interior witness, full mixed-sign branch geometry, and tolerance-certified optimizer sets.

sampling_model.design: For each \(\rho\in I\), independently across every \(s\in S\), draw a simple-random fixed-size holdout and a balanced complete-randomization stage-one assignment. Compute the full signed cell \(C\in\{0,1\}^S\), recruit exactly its positive coordinates, and then independently completely randomize stage two only in recruited strata. The Fisher reference rerandomizes the joint augmented first action, recomputes the entire selector, restricts to the same \(C\), and then draws the appropriate stage-two product kernel.
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite-population triangular array over two stages and an arbitrary fixed finite nonempty set of strata; assignment and holdout randomization are the only sources of randomness. The explicit array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) is a two-stratum subcase used only as the negative-discrepancy witness.
sampling_model.treatment: Balanced binary treatment is completely randomized in every stage-one stratum and, after recruitment, in every selected stage-two stratum under its history-conditional kernel. Holdout status augments the first randomized action but does not alter potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment quotas have positive limiting shares, represented complete signed cells have the fixed positive sampling and reference margins, and the limiting conditional residual variance is at least \(\rho_0\). All products and minima range over fixed finite \(S\) and \(J\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Random complement counts, the complement Neyman studentizer, normalized-midrank studentizers, pair-spacing slopes, and mean--rank correlations are controlled jointly in the finite-population transfer. Maximum influence is derived from the fourth-moment, variance-margin, and share primitives; no Gaussian limit is assumed.

prose_updates.related_work: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao's Definition 1 and Propositions 1--2 provide the broader adaptive-experiment representation specialized here. The exact map uses stage-one population \(\mathcal R_1\), augmented action \(D,Z_1\), selector \(\mathcal S_1=C\), selected population \(\mathcal R_2(C)\), and a constant sharp-null schedule \(\mathcal G\). Their Proposition 1 yields validity without imputability; A2--A3 in Proposition 2 yield the conditional-law representation, and A1 plus imputability yield computability. This is a specialization, not class equivalence, and their broader \(K\)-stage class supplies no selected Gaussian power frontier. Li and Ding supply the finite-population vector central limit theorem used after the present influence bounds. Shenfeld and van Handel supply Ehrhard--Borell convexity and equality cases. Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu are a nonnested architectural comparator: their normal model-based policies optimize expected sample size and familywise error rather than exact complete-cell conditional-randomization local power, so no optimality theorem transfers. Chen and Andrews concern parametric Gaussian adaptive experiments rather than fixed finite populations.
prose_updates.interpretation: The result separates a reusable exact-inference layer from a new design layer. The augmented-action map certifies that the finite reference is a computable specialization of established selective randomization inference at the sharp null. The Gaussian transfer and the ensuing endpoint, interior, and mixed-sign optimizer geometry are additional results, valid uniformly over a common scalar holdout and finitely many active complete-cell coordinates.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The per-array transfer remains qualitative: it controls random complement counts, studentizers, local rank crossings, complete signed-cell conditioning, null imputation, and moving critical values with one \(\eta_n(B)\), but supplies no deterministic rate uniform over all baseline arrays. Finiteness of \(S\) and \(J\) is essential to the joint Cramér--Wold, finite-product cancellation, common margin, and semianalytic refinement arguments. The FZG bridge establishes only representation, computability, and validity; it does not imply the Gaussian approximation or any holdout-power optimum. The two-component mixture remains deliberately two-stratum and certifies interiority, not uniqueness.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The strata may form any fixed finite nonempty set, but may not grow with \(n\). The common scalar holdout is chosen from the fixed compact interval \(I\), and only active pairs in finite \(J\) are tested. Finite-sample exactness is confined to the prespecified Fisher sharp-zero null. Positive local alternatives use a shifted sampling law, while each realized dataset creates a separate zero-drift Fisher reference. The FZG relationship is a specialization of their augmented-action representation, not class equivalence; their results do not supply this note's Gaussian transfer or optimizer. Rosenblum--Fang--Liu is nonnested and transfers no optimality claim. The explicit \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) witness sets \(S=\{1,2\}\) only for that counterexample. General outputs remain set-valued unless an explicit separation certificate proves a unique design.
